name: Australian Communications and Media Authority
role: Federal online gambling enforcement. Australian state and territory authorities issue the wagering licences listed by ACMA.
coverage: The ACMA export lists trading names and their licence holders. Some holders appear under several names, and a listing may describe a telephone-only or inactive service. Current-licence flags require a separate match on the Northern Territory licensing register. The selected domestic BetStop investigations and signed offshore warnings are an illustrative case series. One investigation can cover multiple services or sanctions. Public outcome dates for domestic cases and signed dates for offshore warnings are identified separately. Website-blocking requests concern specified services and are excluded from named-entity case counts. A national enforcement rate would require a matched reporting period and eligible population; this register also excludes unlicensed offshore services investigated by ACMA.

blocking_example.summary: ACMA named Gday77, SpinBet and X4Bet in a request to internet service providers. The announcement identifies services and supplies no legal-entity determination for these rows.

actions.title: Picklebet accepted wagers from a self-excluded customer
actions.summary: The provider accepted bets on 9 February 2026 after the customer joined BetStop. Other allegations about account closure and marketing did not result in breach findings in this investigation.
actions.start_basis: The formal ACMA investigation opening is recorded in paragraph 2 of the investigation report. The outcome date shown is ACMA’s public announcement.

actions.title: Palmerbet agreed to review its self-exclusion controls
actions.summary: The company accepted 312 bets from one self-excluded customer and repaid deposits. Its 18-month undertaking includes an independent compliance review.
actions.start_basis: The formal ACMA investigation opening is recorded in paragraph 1 of the investigation report. The outcome date shown is ACMA’s public announcement.

actions.title: Dabble penalties for BetStop account and messaging breaches
actions.summary: ACMA reported 157 accounts that should have been closed and 839 electronic messages sent to 165 self-excluded people. The total paid covers multiple notices in this one investigation.
actions.start_basis: The formal ACMA investigation opening is recorded in paragraph 2 of the investigation report. The outcome date shown is ACMA’s public announcement.

actions.title: Entain undertaking over Ladbrokes and Neds self-exclusion controls
actions.summary: ACMA found failures to link or close customer accounts and breaches involving new accounts, wagers and BetStop messaging. The undertaking requires an independent review over 18 months.
actions.start_basis: The formal ACMA investigation opening is recorded in paragraph 1 of the investigation report. The outcome date shown is ACMA’s public announcement.

actions.title: Lucky Dreams formal warning
actions.summary: The notice identified Dama as the provider of an unlicensed regulated gambling service with an Australian customer link. The action applies to its Australian offering.
actions.start_basis: Investigation opened on the date stated in the signed statutory warning. The outcome date is the date printed on the warning.

actions.title: Tabcorp penalty for providing wagering services to self-excluded customers
actions.summary: ACMA found two accounts were opened and wagering services were provided to registered customers on 47 days. The undertaking covers verification processes and staff training.
actions.start_basis: The formal ACMA investigation opening is recorded in paragraph 1 of the investigation report. The outcome date shown is ACMA’s public announcement.

actions.title: Fortune Play formal warning
actions.summary: The warning identifies Dama as the service provider and covers both prohibited and unlicensed regulated services offered to Australian customers.
actions.start_basis: Investigation opened on the date stated in the signed statutory warning. The outcome date is the date printed on the warning.

actions.title: Unibet penalty for retaining self-excluded customers’ accounts
actions.summary: ACMA reported delayed closure for 954 accounts. Customers could not place bets during self-exclusion; 45 later used old accounts that should have been closed. A two-year undertaking requires an independent review.
actions.start_basis: The formal ACMA investigation opening is recorded in paragraph 3 of the investigation report. The outcome date shown is ACMA’s public announcement.

actions.title: Crown Slots formal warning
actions.summary: The signed notice names Hollycorn as the provider of an online casino service available to customers in Australia and records a prohibited-service finding.
actions.start_basis: Investigation opened on the date stated in the signed statutory warning. The outcome date is the date printed on the warning.

actions.title: Lucky Hunter and John Vegas Casino formal warning
actions.summary: One statutory warning covers both named online casino services. ACMA attributed their provision to Hollycorn and found an Australian customer link.
actions.start_basis: Investigation opened on the date stated in the signed statutory warning. The outcome date is the date printed on the warning.

actions.title: Lukki Casino formal warning
actions.summary: ACMA named Dama as the provider of a prohibited interactive gambling service with an Australian customer link.
actions.start_basis: Investigation opened on the date stated in the signed statutory warning. The outcome date is the date printed on the warning.

actions.title: Neon 54, Rabona, 5 Gringos and Alf Casino formal warning
actions.summary: The warning covers four named services following one investigation. The instrument records prohibited and unlicensed regulated gambling findings against Rabidi.
actions.start_basis: Investigation opened on the date stated in the signed statutory warning. The outcome date is the date printed on the warning.
